sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是99%无形隐匿。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: When you crank the gear of a music box, you can make the tune go as fast or as slowly as you want,
sentences.zh: 当你转动八音盒的齿轮时，你可以让曲调按你想要的快慢进行，

sentences.en: as you spin the little handle around and around and around.
sentences.zh: 随着你一遍又一遍地转动那个小手柄。

sentences.en: The music is read from this series of little bumps, like Braille.
sentences.zh: 音乐是通过这一系列小突起读取的，就像盲文一样。

sentences.en: Producer Avery Truffleman.
sentences.zh: 制作人艾弗里·特鲁弗曼。

sentences.en: These little bumps stick up and they hit a series of tines, which create a song.
sentences.zh: 这些小突起凸出来，撞击一系列音条，从而创造出一首歌。

sentences.en: It's a form of storage.
sentences.zh: 这是一种存储形式。

sentences.en: This is Dag Spicer, senior curator at the Computer History Museum.
sentences.zh: 我是计算机历史博物馆的高级策展人达格·斯派瑟。

sentences.en: The music box is storing that program, which is the music.
sentences.zh: 八音盒存储了那个程序，也就是音乐。

sentences.en: You think of that as software, even though you might not think of it as that, but that's really what it is.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为那是软件，尽管你可能不会那样想，但它确实就是那个东西。

sentences.en: It's software.
sentences.zh: 它就是软件。

sentences.en: And this method of data storage, a series of bumps or a series of holes, was also used in player pianos.
sentences.zh: 这种数据存储方法，即一系列突起或一系列孔洞，也被用于自动钢琴中。

sentences.en: It's also the mechanism behind computer punch cards.
sentences.zh: 这也是计算机打孔卡背后的机制。

sentences.en: Go ask your grandpa about those.
sentences.zh: 去问问你爷爷关于那些东西的事吧。

sentences.en: Throughout most of the 20th century, punch cards were the dominant form of data processing input and output form.
sentences.zh: 在整个20世纪的大部分时间里，打孔卡是数据处理输入和输出的主要形式。

sentences.en: Paper punch card technology, the precursor to electronic computing, was the way that data was stored and tabulated for decades,
sentences.zh: 纸质打孔卡技术是电子计算的前身，在几十年的时间里一直是存储和制表数据的方式，

sentences.en: back when computers would take up a whole room.
sentences.zh: 回到当时计算机还要占据一整间屋子的年代。

sentences.en: This technology of bumps and holes is also why you're wearing what you're wearing.
sentences.zh: 这种凸起和孔洞的技术也是你现在身上穿着这身衣服的原因。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, one of the things you may not know is that an early automated weaving machine actually has a role to play in the history of computing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可能不知道的一件事是，早期的一台自动织布机实际上在计算历史中扮演了一个角色。

sentences.en: When he says a weaving machine, Dagg is talking about a loom.
sentences.zh: 当他说织布机时，达格指的是一台织机。

sentences.en: A loom is gigantic.
sentences.zh: 织机是巨大的。

sentences.en: Well, there are lots of different kinds of looms and different sizes, but yes, European industrial looms in the 1700s were really big.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有许多不同种类和不同尺寸的织机，但是的，18世纪的欧洲工业织机确实非常大。

sentences.en: About 30 feet high in some cases and maybe 30 feet long.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下大约有30英尺高，可能还有30英尺长。

sentences.en: And it's an enormous, enormous piece of equipment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其巨大的设备。

sentences.en: The design in a fabric is determined by how many threads the weaver goes over or under, which ones come to the top and which ones are submerged in the weave.
sentences.zh: 织物中的设计取决于织工穿过或穿过多少根线，哪几根浮在上面，哪几根沉在织法下面。

sentences.en: These patterns were so complicated and intricate, industrial weavers needed to hire little delicate fingers to pull the threads and keep track of them.
sentences.zh: 这些图案如此复杂繁复，以至于工业织工需要雇佣娇小灵巧的手指来拉动线并留意它们。

sentences.en: And so in the 17th century, this was a job for the draw boy, an actual boy.
sentences.zh: 所以在17世纪，这是提综童工的工作，一个真正的男孩。

sentences.en: So your draw boy would go and say, well, we need to have the white showing through here.
sentences.zh: 所以你的提综童工会过去说，好吧，我们需要在这里露出白色的部分。

sentences.en: So I pull this one.
sentences.zh: 所以我拉这根。

sentences.en: This one needs to go all the way through, but this one needs to be skipped and on and on.
sentences.zh: 这根需要一直穿过去，但这根需要跳过，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So he's pulling these threads.
sentences.zh: 所以他在拉这些线。

sentences.en: This is Chris Garcia, also a curator at the Computer History Museum.
sentences.zh: 这是克里斯·加西亚，同样是计算机历史博物馆的策展人。

sentences.en: It must have been murder on fingers.
sentences.zh: 这对手指来说简直是折磨。

sentences.en: Well, there were tools created to help the draw boys, like forks and levers and harnesses.
sentences.zh: 嗯，人们创造了帮助提综童工的工具，比如叉子、杠杆和吊具。

sentences.en: It wasn't all done with bare hands, but it was a lot of work to do.
sentences.zh: 并不是全凭双手完成的，但那确实需要大量的工作。

sentences.en: You could imagine if you have a significantly large item, you might have 200 threads that have to be pulled.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，如果你有一个相当大的物件，你可能会有200根线必须被拉动。

sentences.en: At the beginning of the 18th century, clothes imported from China became all the rage in France, and a fashion developed for beautiful, tiny, ornate weavings.
sentences.zh: 在18世纪初，从中国进口的服装在法国风靡一时，并且发展出了一种追求美丽、微小、华丽织物的时尚。

sentences.en: Making clothes that are a little bit finer, a little bit more interesting to look at, you can use a jacquard loom to create patterns, sophisticated patterns in that clothing.
sentences.zh: 制作更精细一点、更有看头的衣服，你可以用提花织机在服装中创造图案、复杂的图案。

sentences.en: The jacquard loom was a device, innovated by Joseph Marie Jacquard in 1804.
sentences.zh: 提花织机是约瑟夫·玛丽·雅卡尔于1804年创新的一台设备。

sentences.en: This is an add-on.
sentences.zh: 这是一个附加装置。

sentences.en: And you could attach it to the power loom.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它连接到动力织机上。

sentences.en: So it's like adding cruise control to your car or something.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像给你的汽车添加巡航定速或者类似的东西。

sentences.en: It's like an added feature, so that the work product, the clothes you can produce are even more elaborate.
sentences.zh: 它就像一个附加功能，这样劳动产品，你生产的衣服就能更加精致。

sentences.en: Each new fabric design was encoded in thick cardboard cards.
sentences.zh: 每一个新的织物设计都被编码在厚厚的纸板卡片中。

sentences.en: Each hole, or position of the hole, represents a hook on the loom.
sentences.zh: 每一个孔或孔的位置代表织机上的一个钩子。

sentences.en: A hole in the card told the loom, yes, lift this thread.
sentences.zh: 卡片上的一个孔告诉织机，是的，提起这根线。

sentences.en: So whether the hook is raised or lowered depends on whether there's a hole or not a hole in the jacquard control cards.
sentences.zh: 因此，钩子是升起还是放下，取决于提花控制卡上是否有孔。

sentences.en: Which were tied together into a loop, and fed automatically into the loom.
sentences.zh: 这些卡片被连成一个环，并自动送入织机中。

sentences.en: And one card represented just one pass of thread, so there would be lots of cards sewed together.
sentences.zh: 一张卡片只代表一遍走线，所以会有许多卡片缝合在一起。

sentences.en: And the loop of cards went around and around and around to create a repeating pattern.
sentences.zh: 卡片环周而复始地转动，以创造重复的图案。

sentences.en: Just like the music encoded in the music box.
sentences.zh: 就像编码在八音盒里的音乐一样。

sentences.en: This didn't mean the machine was weaving the cloth automatically.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着机器在自动织布。

sentences.en: It still required a master weaver and a pattern designer and a punch card maker.
sentences.zh: 它仍然需要主织工、图案设计员和打孔卡制作员。

sentences.en: But it did mean the drawboys were out of a job.
sentences.zh: 但它确实意味着提综童工失业了。

sentences.en: Once you have a jacquard mechanism, you don't need the drawboy.
sentences.zh: 一旦你有了提花机构，你就不需要提综童工了。

sentences.en: Half of your workforce can be eliminated.
sentences.zh: 你一半的劳动力都可以被淘汰。

sentences.en: For manufacturers who wanted to make the most beautiful, the most intricate patterns,
sentences.zh: 对于想要制作最美丽、最繁复图案的制造商来说，

sentences.en: what was increasingly more important than labor was intellectual property.
sentences.zh: 比劳动力更重要的东西日益演变成知识产权。

sentences.en: The designs.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些设计。

sentences.en: In jacquard's time, people stole these control cards.
sentences.zh: 在雅卡尔的时代，人们会偷这些控制卡。

sentences.en: Because they represented patterns.
sentences.zh: 因为它们代表了图案。

sentences.en: That if the patterns were popular, it could be very lucrative to keep making.
sentences.zh: 如果这些图案很受欢迎，继续生产它们将会非常赚钱。

sentences.en: You know how fashion goes in styles and everybody comes out with the same stuff every year.
sentences.zh: 你知道时尚是如何遵循潮流的，每年每个人都会推出相同的东西。

sentences.en: Like they're all copying each other almost, right?
sentences.zh: 就像他们几乎都在互相抄袭，对吧？

sentences.en: The same trends.
sentences.zh: 同样的趋势。

sentences.en: So I like to think of this as the first instance of software piracy.
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢把这看作软件盗版的第一个实例。

sentences.en: That people are stealing these jacquard loom cards.
sentences.zh: 人们在偷这些提花织机卡。

sentences.en: And the jacquard loom cards would lead to the development of an entire new industry that would change the world.
sentences.zh: 而提花织机卡将促成一个全新产业的发展，从而改变世界。

sentences.en: a German-American inventor named Herman Hollerith devised a solution to the United States Census Bureau's problem of counting all the new immigrants to the country and citizens.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫赫尔曼·霍勒瑞特的德裔美国发明家设计了一个解决方案，来解决美国人口普查局统计全国所有新移民和公民的问题。

sentences.en: Tabulating the census used to take about 10 years.
sentences.zh: 过去，对人口普查进行制表大约需要10年时间。

sentences.en: So that means by the time the census was finished, it was already time to start taking the next one.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当人口普查完成时，已经到了开始进行下一次普查的时候了。

sentences.en: Hollerith came up with a system where if each individual's information was punched on cards, it could be processed more quickly.
sentences.zh: 霍勒瑞特想出了一种系统，如果把每个人的信息打在卡片上，就能更快地进行处理。

sentences.en: Herman Hollerith specifically quoted the jacquard loom as his influence.
sentences.zh: 赫尔曼·霍勒瑞特明确引用提花织机作为他的影响来源。

sentences.en: His influence for coming up with computer punch cards.
sentences.zh: 他发明计算机打孔卡的灵感来源。

sentences.en: Once you have patterns of holes in a card, it's now machine-readable.
sentences.zh: 一旦卡片上有了孔洞图案，它就变成机器可读的了。

sentences.en: And that's how the census was done in three years instead of 10.
sentences.zh: 这就是人口普查在三年内而不是十年内完成的方式。

sentences.en: The 1890 census was a huge advance in the history of computing.
sentences.zh: 1890年的人口普查是计算历史上的一个巨大进步。

sentences.en: Now, just to wrap up the story, Hollerith's punch card patents were actually the foundation for a small company you may have heard of called International Business Machines,
sentences.zh: 好了，为了总结这个故事，霍勒瑞特的打孔卡专利实际上是一家你可能听说过的小公司的基础，名叫国际商业机器公司，

sentences.en: or IBM.
sentences.zh: 也就是IBM。

sentences.en: Which in some ways owes its existence to the loom, and to that rising demand for beautiful, ornate patterns.
sentences.zh: 从某些方面来说，它的存在要归功于织机，以及对美丽、繁复图案不断上升的需求。

sentences.en: Because of fashion.
sentences.zh: 因为时尚。

sentences.en: Because of fashion.
sentences.zh: 因为时尚。

sentences.en: Fashion is just another word for the constant inevitable shifts in popular taste.
sentences.zh: 时尚只是大众审美品味不断且不可避免的变化的另一个代名词。

sentences.en: Garments, just like buildings and cars and movies, can't help but reflect the circumstances of our moment in history.
sentences.zh: 服装就像建筑、汽车和电影一样，情不自禁地反映了我们历史时刻的环境。

sentences.en: That's what fashion is.
sentences.zh: 这就是时尚。

sentences.en: Another way of telling time.
sentences.zh: 另一种记录时间的方式。

sentences.en: Back and forth.
sentences.zh: 来回往复。

sentences.en: And back and forth.
sentences.zh: 来回往复。

sentences.en: Around and around and around.
sentences.zh: 周而复始。

sentences.en: The loom inspired us the computer.
sentences.zh: 织机启发了我们发明计算机。

sentences.en: The computer changes the way we buy, order, and think about clothes.
sentences.zh: 计算机改变了我们购买、订购和思考衣服的方式。

sentences.en: Clothing and culture impact each other.
sentences.zh: 服装与文化相互影响。

sentences.en: And we need to dedicate some serious time to talking about what we wear.
sentences.zh: 我们需要花一些严肃的时间来谈谈我们穿什么。

sentences.en: So that's what we're going to do.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们要做的。

sentences.en: For the past eight years, we've asked you to start noticing elements in architecture and design.
sentences.zh: 在过去的八年里，我们一直要求你开始注意到建筑和设计中的元素。

sentences.en: Because architecture is the art we live in.
sentences.zh: 因为建筑是我们居住的艺术。

sentences.en: The medium in which we move.
sentences.zh: 我们身处其中的媒介。

sentences.en: Influencing us in a thousand invisible ways.
sentences.zh: 以一千种无形的方式影响着我们。

sentences.en: For the next three weeks, we're going to ask you to do the same.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的三周里，我们将要求你做同样的事情。

sentences.en: With another universal art that we all live in.
sentences.zh: 通过我们都生活其中的另一种普遍艺术。

sentences.en: Clothing.
sentences.zh: 服装。

sentences.en: It's our first spinoff show, hosted by Avery, called Articles of IntereSt.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的第一个衍生节目，由艾弗里主持，名为《趣物志》。

sentences.en: And it will be right here, twice a week, for the next three weeks in your 99PI feed.
sentences.zh: 它将在这儿播出，在接下来的三周内，每周两次出现在你的99PI动态里。

sentences.en: We'll have the first episode after this break, about what happened to working children, like those drawboys, and how their clothing changed.
sentences.zh: 我们将在这次休息后播出第一集，内容关于那些童工（比如提综童工）经历了什么，以及他们的服装是如何改变的。

sentences.en: Like, so what are you wearing right now?
sentences.zh: 比如，你现在身上穿的是什么？

sentences.en: Oh, jeez.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So what I'm wearing now, this is a black shirt from, like, American Apparel.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在穿的，这是一件来自比如American Apparel的黑色衬衫。

sentences.en: And it's like a f***ing god fabric.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一块他妈的神仙面料。

sentences.en: I can't explain it.
sentences.zh: 我无法解释它。

sentences.en: My friend and colleague Joe Rosenberg is a really good dresser.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友兼同事乔·罗森伯格是个很会穿衣服的人。

sentences.en: He just has this rich understanding of textiles and cuts.
sentences.zh: 他对纺织品和剪裁有着丰富的理解。

sentences.en: And you can just tell in all these subtle ways.
sentences.zh: 你可以从所有这些微妙的方面看出来。

sentences.en: Below that is seven-for-all-mankind jeans.
sentences.zh: 里面那是7forallmankind的牛仔裤。

sentences.en: They make pretty good kid-sized jeans, which is what I wear.
sentences.zh: 他们生产相当不错的儿童尺码牛仔裤，这也是我穿的。

sentences.en: Joe shops in kid sizes.
sentences.zh: 乔买的是儿童尺码。

sentences.en: I'm four foot eight.
sentences.zh: 我身高四尺八（约1米42）。

sentences.en: I guess you could say I'm a little person insofar as I am literally little.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以说我是个小矮人，就字面意义上的矮而言。

sentences.en: But, um, I don't think of myself in that way.
sentences.zh: 但是，嗯，我并不那样看待自己。

sentences.en: I'm just the size of a ten-year-old.
sentences.zh: 我只是个十岁小孩的身高。

sentences.en: Joe doesn't have the typical dimensions of someone with dwarfism.
sentences.zh: 乔并不具备侏儒症患者的典型体型尺寸。

sentences.en: So it's called, and I'm going to botch the pronunciation, it's called spondyloepiphythial dysplasia.
sentences.zh: 所以它被称为——我要把发音给搞砸了——它被称为脊椎骨骺发育不良。

sentences.en: It's a mutation that I developed as an embryo.
sentences.zh: 这是我在胚胎时期产生的一种突变。

sentences.en: To demonstrate how rare it is, like, I mean, my entire life I've only had one occasion to meet someone who was my height and was short in the way I was short.
sentences.zh: 为了说明它有多罕见，我是说，我的一生中只有一次机会遇到一个身高和我一样、并且在矮的方式上和我一样的人。

sentences.en: I was at a party in college, senior year of college.
sentences.zh: 我在大学的一个派对上，大四的时候。

sentences.en: I still remember it.
sentences.zh: 我仍然记得。

sentences.en: And we talked about, we talked about clothes.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论了，我们谈论了衣服。

sentences.en: Articles of Interest, a show about what we wear.
sentences.zh: 《趣物志》，一档关于我们穿什么的节目。

sentences.en: And so maybe the ideas about clothes.
sentences.zh: 所以也许关于衣服的观念。

sentences.en: You can attach.
sentences.zh: 你可以附加。

sentences.en: Our ideas about class.
sentences.zh: 我们关于阶级的观念。

sentences.en: An idea of home to a piece of cloth.
sentences.zh: 家的观念寄托在一块布料上。

sentences.en: These are best for laSt.
sentences.zh: 这些留到最后最合适。

sentences.en: Any fool can wear clothes.
sentences.zh: 任何傻瓜都能穿衣服。

sentences.en: But if you ain't got the attitude and style to carry it off, man, you're just a clothes boss.
sentences.zh: 但如果你没有那种气场和风格来驾驭它，伙计，你只是个衣服架子。

sentences.en: Clothes are records of the bodies we've lived in.
sentences.zh: 衣服是我们曾栖居过的身体的记录。

sentences.en: Think of an old sweater you used to have that's just not your style anymore.
sentences.zh: 想想你以前有一件旧毛衣，只是不再符合你的风格了。

sentences.en: Or jeans that just aren't your size anymore.
sentences.zh: 或者不再适合你尺码的牛仔裤。

sentences.en: We are like snakes who shed our skins and grow new ones as we age.
sentences.zh: 我们就像蛇一样，随着年龄的增长，蜕去旧皮，长出新皮。

sentences.en: And it all starts in the kids' department.
sentences.zh: 这一切都始于儿童服装部。

sentences.en: It's not looking good.
sentences.zh: 情况不妙。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: Joe and I went to J.Crew together.
sentences.zh: 我和乔一起去了J.Crew。

sentences.en: He was pretty much ready to give up as soon as we walked in.
sentences.zh: 我们一走进去，他基本上就准备放弃了。

sentences.en: We haven't even dove in yet.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至都还没深入进去呢。

sentences.en: I know we haven't.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们还没呢。

sentences.en: The kids' section was one row.
sentences.zh: 儿童区只有一排。

sentences.en: And everything in it was very loud.
sentences.zh: 而且上面的每样东西声音都很大。

sentences.en: This shirt glows in the dark.
sentences.zh: 这件衬衫会在黑暗中发光。

sentences.en: This shirt glows in the dark.
sentences.zh: 这件衬衫会在黑暗中发光。

sentences.en: This shirt has many tie-dye bicycles on it.
sentences.zh: 这件衬衫上面有许多扎染的自行车图案。

sentences.en: This shirt has so many stripes that maybe it almost works.
sentences.zh: 这件衬衫有太多的条纹，也许它居然还挺搭的。

sentences.en: The color palette of the children's department tends to be really bright and way over-decorated,
sentences.zh: 儿童服装部门的色调往往非常鲜艳，而且过度装饰，

sentences.en: as Joe and I debriefed in his car.
sentences.zh: 正如乔和我当时在他的车里复盘时所说的那样。

sentences.en: The fundamental thing about shopping as a very short person having to shop for kids' clothes is that your life is just this hellscape of, like,
sentences.zh: 作为一个身材非常矮小、不得不买童装的人，购物最根本的问题在于，你的生活简直就是人间炼狱，比如：

sentences.en: ripped jeans and deliberate patches and fun slogans and crazy zippers and bold colors and prints.
sentences.zh: 破洞牛仔裤、刻意缝上的补丁、有趣的标语、疯狂的拉链以及大胆的颜色和印花。

sentences.en: And the idea that you're going to find just, like, slim jeans in a subtle hue, dark wash, you know, like, no.
sentences.zh: 至于你想找那种色调低调、深水洗的修身牛仔裤……你知道的，想都别想。

sentences.en: It just doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 根本找不到。

sentences.en: It almost makes no sense.
sentences.zh: 这简直毫无道理。

sentences.en: But no.
sentences.zh: 但事实就是没有。

sentences.en: All that decoration and phony self-expression is put in a blender with birthday cake and sequins and then put in a hanger on a rack.
sentences.zh: 所有这些装饰和虚假的自我表达，就像被放进搅拌机里和生日蛋糕、亮片混在一起，然后挂在衣架上。

sentences.en: That's the kids' section.
sentences.zh: 这就是童装区。

sentences.en: It's bad.
sentences.zh: 这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: It's really bad.
sentences.zh: 真的太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And actually, even if I'm just alone, I'm, like, slightly embarrassed for myself.
sentences.zh: 说实话，哪怕只有我一个人，我也会觉得有点替自己不好意思。

sentences.en: So how did we get here?
sentences.zh: 那么我们是怎么走到这一步的呢？

sentences.en: Where did the style we call children's clothes come from?
sentences.zh: 我们所说的童装风格究竟是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: Children's clothes haven't always been a thing.
sentences.zh: 童装并不是一直都存在的。

sentences.en: And historically, especially in the United States, childhood itself was a luxury.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，尤其是在美国，童年本身就是一种奢侈。

sentences.en: Because you have working children, children of parents who are not slaves but have to work,
sentences.zh: 因为当时有童工，有那些父母不是奴隶但必须工作的儿童，

sentences.en: and the children who are slaves and have to work and maybe don't have a childhood much really at all.
sentences.zh: 还有那些身为奴隶必须工作的儿童，他们可能根本谈不上有什么真正的童年。

sentences.en: This is Erin Algeo.
sentences.zh: 这是艾琳·阿尔热（Erin Algeo）。

sentences.en: She's the curator at the La Cisse Museum of Lace and Textiles in Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 她是伯克利拉西斯蕾丝与纺织品博物馆的馆长。

sentences.en: Some children are always clean and some children are always precious and some are not.
sentences.zh: 有些孩子总是干干净净，有些孩子总是备受珍视，而有些则不然。

sentences.en: That's class.
sentences.zh: 这就是阶级。

sentences.en: That's whether someone is slave or free.
sentences.zh: 这就是一个人是奴隶还是自由身地区别的体现。

sentences.en: The children who were not considered clean or precious didn't get children's clothes.
sentences.zh: 那些不被认为干净或珍贵的儿童是没有童装可穿的。

sentences.en: I'm sure you've seen pictures of children that are working.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定你见过童工的照片。

sentences.en: And they do look like little adults as they're standing in the cotton mill or boys that go down and work in the mines.
sentences.zh: 当他们站在棉纺厂里，或者作为小男孩下矿井工作时，看起来确实像个小大人。

sentences.en: Basically, poorer children were given what was around.
sentences.zh: 基本上，较贫穷的孩子穿的都是身边有什么就穿什么。

sentences.en: While upper-class children had the privilege of being deliberately dressed.
sentences.zh: 而上流社会的儿童则享有被精心打扮的特权。

sentences.en: And although fancy children were also sometimes dressed like little adults, underneath their clothes, a lot of them were wearing corsets.
sentences.zh: 虽然有钱人家的孩子有时也会被装扮得像小大人一样，但他们的衣服里面，很多人其实都穿着束腰胸衣。

sentences.en: If your parents wanted to raise you correctly, they would put you boys and girls in corsets.
sentences.zh: 如果你的父母想把你好好抚养长大，他们就会让你——无论男孩还是女孩——穿上胸衣。

sentences.en: There's this whole idea that children had to be cultivated, like a dog in a harness or a flower on a trellis.
sentences.zh: 当时普遍有这样一种观念：必须对儿童进行塑形，就像用背带拴住狗或者在格子架上修剪花朵一样。

sentences.en: Now, the corsets were not as intense as older women wore.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些胸衣不像成年女性穿的那么紧绷。

sentences.en: But yes, boys and girls, it was considered for posture and so forth that you would be in a corset.
sentences.zh: 但没错，无论是男孩还是女孩，为了仪态等原因，人们认为你是应该穿胸衣的。

sentences.en: And although it happened slowly, the demise of the child corset is thanks to philosophers like Jean-Jacques Rousseau.
sentences.zh: 尽管这个过程很缓慢，但儿童胸衣的消亡要归功于让-雅克·卢梭这样的哲学家。

sentences.en: Our concept of childhood that we have now was really formed in the 18th century.
sentences.zh: 我们现在所拥有的童年概念，实际上是在18世纪形成的。

sentences.en: In 1762, Rousseau wrote,
sentences.zh: 在1762年，卢梭写道：

sentences.en: Hold childhood in reverence and do not be in any hurry to judge it for good or for ill.
sentences.zh: “敬畏童年，不要急于对它的好坏做出评判。”

sentences.en: Give nature time to work before you take over her business, lest you interfere with her dealings.
sentences.zh: “在接手大自然的工作之前，给自然留出发挥作用的时间，以免干预她的运作。”

sentences.en: It made the concept that those little bodies needed to be free, free and unfettered.
sentences.zh: 这就确立了一种观念：那些小小的身体需要获得自由，自由且无拘无束。

sentences.en: Side note, Rousseau himself was a terrible dad.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，卢梭本人是个糟糕的父亲。

sentences.en: He dropped his children off at an orphanage and abandoned them.
sentences.zh: 他把自己的孩子送去了孤儿院并遗弃了他们。

sentences.en: But philosophies like his, paired with eventual child labor laws and regulations,
sentences.zh: 但像他这样的哲学思想，再加上后来的童工法律和法规，

sentences.en: really helped shape our idea of what a precious, valuable time childhood is.
sentences.zh: 确实帮助塑造了我们对童年是多么宝贵、多么有价值的时代这一认知。

sentences.en: In the 18th century, clothes just for children come in and they look different than adult clothes.
sentences.zh: 在18世纪，专为儿童设计的服装出现了，它们看起来与成人服装不同。

sentences.en: In these clothes, children are dressed up for the occasion of their youth.
sentences.zh: 穿着这些衣服的孩子们，是为了庆祝他们的青春年少而盛装打扮的。

sentences.en: This amazing time free from cares, separate from the rest of their lives.
sentences.zh: 这是一个美妙的、无忧无虑、与他们生活其余部分相隔离的时代。

sentences.en: They were designed for ease of movement.
sentences.zh: 它们的剪裁是为了方便活动。

sentences.en: When we look at them today, we can't believe anyone could move in them.
sentences.zh: 今天当我们看到这些服装时，简直不敢相信居然有人能穿着它们活动。

sentences.en: They may have been easier to move in than a corset, but these clothes were still really formal,
sentences.zh: 它们可能比胸衣更容易活动，但这些服装其实依然非常正式，

sentences.en: like embroidered dresses for girls and boxy little suits for boys.
sentences.zh: 比如女孩穿的刺绣连衣裙和男孩穿的方正小西装。

sentences.en: But it just looks like a little suit, I guess.
sentences.zh: 不过我猜，它看起来就像一套小西装。

sentences.en: Adorable.
sentences.zh: 太可爱了。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, it is adorable, actually.
sentences.zh: 对，没错，其实真的很可爱。

sentences.en: So children are wearing these adorable mini-me get-ups.
sentences.zh: 所以孩子们穿着这些可爱的缩小版成人套装。

sentences.en: It's almost like a parody of adulthood.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像是对成年人世界的一种戏仿。

sentences.en: Stuff meant to look like adult clothes that adults would never actually wear,
sentences.zh: 那些看起来像是成人服装、但成年人实际上绝不会穿的东西，

sentences.en: which is what we see now in the kids' department.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们现在在童装部看到的那些。

sentences.en: And it has everything to do with our evolving concepts of childhood
sentences.zh: 这一切都与我们不断演变的童年概念息息相关，

sentences.en: and how much freedom and protection we think children ought to have.
sentences.zh: 以及我们认为儿童应该拥有多少自由和保护。

sentences.en: Because although their corsets are long gone,
sentences.zh: 因为尽管他们的胸衣早已不复存在，

sentences.en: children are still bound by legal requirements.
sentences.zh: 但儿童依然受到法律要求的约束。

sentences.en: What is this thing you gave me?
sentences.zh: 你给我的这是什么东西？

sentences.en: This is from the NRA.
sentences.zh: 这是来自NRA的。

sentences.en: No, not that NRA.
sentences.zh: 不，不是那个NRA。

sentences.en: The National Retail Association of Australia.
sentences.zh: 是澳大利亚全国零售协会。

sentences.en: My friend Morgan is not Australian.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友摩根（Morgan）不是澳大利亚人。

sentences.en: She is a technical designer for a big children's clothing company.
sentences.zh: 她是一家大型童装公司的技术设计师。

sentences.en: She'd rather not say which one.
sentences.zh: 她不愿意透露具体是哪家。

sentences.en: One of the major children's clothing retailers in the United States.
sentences.zh: 她是美国主要的童装零售商之一的员工。

sentences.en: Her company has many, many, many rules about what can and cannot be in children's clothes.
sentences.zh: 她的公司对于童装里可以有什么、不可以有什么，有着非常、非常、非常多的规定。

sentences.en: But those rules are top secret.
sentences.zh: 但这些规定是高度机密的。

sentences.en: So Morgan brought me that Australian safety guide
sentences.zh: 所以摩根把那本澳大利亚安全指南拿给我看，

sentences.en: because it's kind of similar and it gives you a rough idea.
sentences.zh: 因为它有点类似，能让你有个大致的概念。

sentences.en: It's 76 pages long and thorough.
sentences.zh: 它有76页厚，非常详尽。

sentences.en: And it goes through at the beginning the way you assess risk,
sentences.zh: 它在开头部分详细讲解了如何评估风险，

sentences.en: which is high to low based on if a kid could die from it.
sentences.zh: 根据孩子是否会因此丧命，风险分为从高到低几档。

sentences.en: You don't want choking hazards, no sharp edges, and no drawstrings.
sentences.zh: 你必须避免窒息隐患、没有锋利的边缘，而且不能有抽绳。

sentences.en: Globally, there are reports of various serious injuries and deaths occurring
sentences.zh: 在全球范围内，有报道称，当结、扣子或绳端被卷入或卡入运动部件或正在关闭的门时，

sentences.en: when knots, toggles, or cord ends become snagged or caught into moving parts or closing doors.
sentences.zh: 会发生各种严重的伤害和死亡事故。

sentences.en: And in order to address that, you can't have a cord that's longer than three inches.
sentences.zh: 为了解决这个问题，绳子的长度不能超过三英寸。

sentences.en: And that goes all the way up to 12 years in the United States.
sentences.zh: 在美国，这一规定甚至适用于12岁以下的儿童。

sentences.en: Sometimes in the kids section, you can see drawstrings on hoodies or sweatpants,
sentences.zh: 有时在童装区，你能看到连帽衫或运动裤上有抽绳，

sentences.en: but those don't actually function.
sentences.zh: 但它们实际上并不起作用。

sentences.en: They're just decorative.
sentences.zh: 它们只是装饰性的。

sentences.en: They can't actually cinch the body.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上并不能收紧衣服。

sentences.en: You can only cinch it in between these two inches.
sentences.zh: 你只能在这两英寸的范围内收紧它。

sentences.en: It's basically so that kids can look like little adults
sentences.zh: 这基本上是为了让孩子们看起来像小大人，

sentences.en: without running the risks of adult dressing.
sentences.zh: 又不用承担成年人穿衣所带来的风险。

sentences.en: So the clothing companies don't get in trouble.
sentences.zh: 这样服装公司就不会惹上麻烦了。

sentences.en: I mean, you can get sued for sure if you kill kids, you know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你弄死了小孩子，你绝对是会被起诉的，你知道的。

sentences.en: They're not doing it just for a sense of morality.
sentences.zh: 他们这么做不仅仅是为了某种道德感。

sentences.en: These guidelines are the cobbled-together aftermath of a series of disasters.
sentences.zh: 这些指南是一系列灾难后拼凑出来的后果。

sentences.en: It's just like lawsuit after lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 就像是一场接一场的诉讼。

sentences.en: Every time an item is recalled or a clothing company gets sued for endangering a child,
sentences.zh: 每当有一款商品被召回，或者一家服装公司因危害儿童而遭到起诉，

sentences.en: the guidelines get revised or tightened.
sentences.zh: 指南就会被修订或收紧。

sentences.en: And one of the biggest legal differences between children and adult clothes is flammability.
sentences.zh: 儿童服装与成人服装在法律上最大的区别之一就是易燃性。

sentences.en: Flame retardant's a huge one.
sentences.zh: 阻燃剂是一个极其重要的指标。

sentences.en: Everything has to be flame retardant if they're sleeping.
sentences.zh: 如果衣服是用来睡觉的，所有东西都必须具备阻燃性。

sentences.en: If a child is going to sleep in it, the fabric has to be flame retardant.
sentences.zh: 如果孩子要穿着它睡觉，面料必须是阻燃的。

sentences.en: And the garment has to fit tight.
sentences.zh: 而且服装必须贴身。

sentences.en: They are concerned about candles, nightlights, fires in-house, whatever could happen.
sentences.zh: 他们担心蜡烛、小夜灯、室内火灾，以及任何可能发生的意外。

sentences.en: If their kid is wearing loose-fitting clothing and it's hanging loose from you,
sentences.zh: 如果他们的孩子穿的是宽松的衣服，衣服松垮地挂在身上，

sentences.en: it's just going to have a lot of oxygen to give you a bunch of third-degree burns.
sentences.zh: 就会有充足的氧气，从而导致严重的三度烧伤。

sentences.en: Anything that could potentially be sleepwear has to be near skin tight
sentences.zh: 任何可能被当作睡衣的衣物都必须极其贴身，

sentences.en: and it has to be flame-resistant so that doesn't happen to kids.
sentences.zh: 并且必须具备阻燃性能，这样才不会对孩子们造成这种伤害。

sentences.en: And this starts to get at our question about why kids' clothes look the way they do.
sentences.zh: 这就开始触及我们的疑问：为什么童装看起来是这个样子的？

sentences.en: Because note how Morgan said anything that could potentially be sleepwear.
sentences.zh: 因为请注意摩根是怎么说的——任何可能被当作睡衣的东西。

sentences.en: Flammability rules don't just apply to clothes labeled as pajamas.
sentences.zh: 阻燃规则不仅适用于贴有睡衣标签的衣服。

sentences.en: They could apply to any garment a parent puts their kids to sleep in.
sentences.zh: 它们可以适用于父母让孩子穿着入睡的任何衣服。

sentences.en: Or that a kid decides that they want to sleep in it.
sentences.zh: 或者孩子自己决定想穿着入睡的衣服。

sentences.en: So anything that is comfortable or soft, which means that kids' clothing, if it's not sleepwear,
sentences.zh: 因此，任何舒适或柔软的东西——这意味着如果童装不是睡衣，

sentences.en: has to go through great pains to prove that it's not sleepwear
sentences.zh: 就必须费尽周折地证明它不是睡衣，

sentences.en: so that they don't have to meet all those flammability and size requirements.
sentences.zh: 这样它们才不必满足所有这些关于阻燃和尺寸的要求。

sentences.en: So let's say you're trying to design kids' clothes that are not for sleeping.
sentences.zh: 所以，假设你正在设计不是用来睡觉的童装。

sentences.en: They can't have pictures of anything that could be interpreted as sleepy.
sentences.zh: 它们不能印有任何会被解释为与睡眠有关的图案。

sentences.en: Like what is pictured on it?
sentences.zh: 比如上面印的是什么？

sentences.en: Is it sleeping animals?
sentences.zh: 是睡觉的动物吗？

sentences.en: Is it a sleepy scene?
sentences.zh: 是一个充满睡意的场景吗？

sentences.en: Does that make you feel sleepy?
sentences.zh: 这会让你感到困倦吗？

sentences.en: If it makes you feel sleepy, it's sleepwear.
sentences.zh: 如果它让你感到困倦，它就是睡衣。

sentences.en: So no images of the moon, no images of stars, and no clouds.
sentences.zh: 所以不能有月亮的图案，不能有星星的图案，也不能有云彩。

sentences.en: You know, like a cloud thing probably wouldn't work.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如云彩图案可能就行不通。

sentences.en: Your legal department at your company would be like, you can't do that because that makes me feel like sleep.
sentences.zh: 你公司的法律部门会说：“你不能这样做，因为这让我感觉像是要睡觉。”

sentences.en: And then certain animals, like owls.
sentences.zh: 然后是一些特定的动物，比如猫头鹰。

sentences.en: Same with other nocturnal creatures like bats.
sentences.zh: 其他夜行动物也是如此，比如蝙蝠。

sentences.en: Unless you're designing a Halloween line and you really, really, really want to have a shirt with a bat on it.
sentences.zh: 除非你正在设计万圣节系列，并且非常、非常、非常想要一件印有蝙蝠的衬衫。

sentences.en: I don't know if it was on Halloween and it had enough sequins on it or something, maybe you could get away with it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，如果它是在万圣节穿的，而且上面有足够多的亮片什么的，也许你能蒙混过关。

sentences.en: Sequins are a good way to show a garment is not for sleeping.
sentences.zh: 亮片是表明一件衣服不是用来睡觉的好方法。

sentences.en: Same with glitter and action graphics and bright colors and ornamental pockets.
sentences.zh: 闪粉、动感印花、鲜艳的颜色和装饰性口袋也是如此。

sentences.en: You could bring it enough out of sleepwear that a kid would never want to sleep on it.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它设计得足够不像是睡衣，让小孩子根本不想穿着它睡觉。

sentences.en: So make it uncomfortable or make it a jacket or something like that.
sentences.zh: 所以，把它做得让人感觉不太舒服，或者把它做成夹克之类的款式。

sentences.en: It's decoration as a form of protection.
sentences.zh: 这就是作为保护形式的装饰。

sentences.en: Defending kids from fire and also protecting the companies from liability.
sentences.zh: 既保护儿童免受火灾侵害，也保护公司免受法律责任的牵连。

sentences.en: Sometimes behind the glitter and garishness is a legal subtext.
sentences.zh: 有时候，亮片和俗艳的外表背后隐藏着法律上的潜台词。

sentences.en: Sometimes.
sentences.zh: 有时候是这样的。

sentences.en: Not all the time.
sentences.zh: 并非总是如此。

sentences.en: No, I would say that they believe that they're giving you something more special, something more marketable by putting tchotchkes on the garment.
sentences.zh: 不，我会说他们相信，通过在服装上添加小玩意，他们是在为你提供更特别、更有市场价值的东西。

sentences.en: This is Lana Hoag, an industry expert who's been working in garment development and production for over 30 years.
sentences.zh: 这是拉娜·霍格（Lana Hoag），一位在服装开发和生产领域工作了30多年的行业专家。

sentences.en: And the sequins are usually to appeal to the child.
sentences.zh: 而亮片通常是为了吸引小孩子。

sentences.en: Do they do a lot of test groups and focus groups with little kids?
sentences.zh: 他们会和小孩子们做很多测试小组和焦点小组调研吗？

sentences.en: You know, I think they should more.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我觉得他们应该多做一些。

sentences.en: I have not seen that anywhere.
sentences.zh: 我没在任何地方见过这种做法。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: I worked.
sentences.zh: 我工作过。

sentences.en: Manufacturers will ask parents what they're looking for in terms of styles, but not the kids themselves.
sentences.zh: 制造商会询问父母他们在款式上有什么要求，但不会直接问孩子们。

sentences.en: They don't have any money.
sentences.zh: 他们又没有钱。

sentences.en: Probably the closest they've come to focus groups and test groups were the photo shoots.
sentences.zh: 他们最接近焦点小组和测试小组的环节，大概就是拍照的时候了。

sentences.en: Well, and fit sessions.
sentences.zh: 还有试穿环节。

sentences.en: We want to see how something fits.
sentences.zh: 我们需要看看衣服合不合身。

sentences.en: But if they're kind of, oh, it's itchy and they want out of it, then you know that that's probably just a special occasion dress.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们表现得像，哦，这衣服扎人，他们想脱下来，那你就知道这可能只是一件特殊场合穿的裙子。

sentences.en: It's not going to be their favorite item.
sentences.zh: 这不会成为他们最喜欢的衣物。

sentences.en: But it's not like you'd cancel a garment because a kid didn't like it.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着会因为小孩子不喜欢就取消生产这件衣服。

sentences.en: No, unfortunately, they don't still.
sentences.zh: 对，遗憾的是，到现在依然如此。

sentences.en: So the loudness of the kids department has to do with safety rules, but not entirely.
sentences.zh: 所以童装区色彩鲜艳喧闹，跟安全规定有关，但又不完全是。

sentences.en: So it's not because of flammability.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是因为防火阻燃的要求。

sentences.en: It's because of what kids want.
sentences.zh: 而是因为孩子们想要什么。

sentences.en: But we don't ask kids what they want.
sentences.zh: 但我们并不问孩子们想要什么。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's what we think kids want.
sentences.zh: 这只是我们以为孩子们想要什么。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: No, I think you're right.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得你说得对。

sentences.en: But if you took a child into the store and you're walking around, a lot of them are drawn to the silly things hanging off a garment, but only up until a certain age.
sentences.zh: 但如果你带着孩子去店里逛，你会发现很多孩子都会被衣服上垂下来的滑稽小物件吸引，不过这也只限于某个年龄段之前。

sentences.en: And I think that kids go through a really awkward period where they're trying to figure out what's cool again because they don't trust their previous tastes.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为孩子们会经历一个非常尴尬的时期，他们试图重新弄清楚什么是酷，因为他们不再相信自己先前的审美了。

sentences.en: Although this is true for anyone at any age.
sentences.zh: 尽管对任何年龄段的人来说这都是一样的。

sentences.en: We move out of one face and into the next.
sentences.zh: 我们告别一个阶段，进入下一个阶段。

sentences.en: Unless you are trapped in the children's section and forever relegated to this bright, loud, strange way of dressing.
sentences.zh: 除非你被困在童装区，永远沦落于这种鲜艳、喧闹又奇怪的穿衣风格。

sentences.en: Look at a piece of paper.
sentences.zh: 看着一张纸。

sentences.en: Words from yesterday.
sentences.zh: 昨日的字句。

sentences.en: There's a portrait painted on the thing we love.
sentences.zh: 在我们所爱的事物上画着一幅肖像。

sentences.en: Articles of Interest was made by myself, Avery Truffleman.
sentences.zh: 《Articles of Interest》由我 Avery Truffleman 制作。

sentences.en: Edited by Joe Rosenberg.
sentences.zh: Joe Rosenberg 编辑。

sentences.en: Music by Ray Royal.
sentences.zh: Ray Royal 配乐。

sentences.en: Intro and outro themes by Sasami Ashworth.
sentences.zh: 片头和片尾主题曲由 Sasami Ashworth 创作。

sentences.en: Fact check by Graham Heysha.
sentences.zh: Graham Heysha 负责事实核查。

sentences.en: Mixed by Kelly Coyne.
sentences.zh: Kelly Coyne 负责混音。

sentences.en: And Roman Mars is the adult supervision of this whole series.
sentences.zh: 而 Roman Mars 是整个系列的成年人监督。

sentences.en: A very special thanks to Cassia St. Clair, Susie Furr, Juliet Heinle, Nehruz Solomon, and the Smitten Mitten Audio Collective in Detroit.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢 Cassia St. Clair、Susie Furr、Juliet Heinle、Nehruz Solomon 以及底特律的 Smitten Mitten 音频集体。

sentences.en: As well as Katie Mingle, Emmett Fitzgerald, Sharif Youssef, Vivian Lee, Delaney Hall, Kurt Colstead, and the whole 99PI team.
sentences.zh: 还要感谢 Katie Mingle、Emmett Fitzgerald、Sharif Youssef、Vivian Lee、Delaney Hall、Kurt Colstead 以及整个 99PI 团队。

sentences.en: When you think of old-timey little kids, one of the main costumes that come to mind is the sailor suit.
sentences.zh: 当你想到老式的小孩时，浮现在脑海中的主要服装之一就是水手服。

sentences.en: Like Donald Duck wore.
sentences.zh: 就像唐老鸭穿的那种。

sentences.en: A little naval costume for the cute little future man.
sentences.zh: 为可爱的小未来男子汉准备的小海军制服。

sentences.en: You're being part of the establishment, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 你这是在融入体制对吧？

sentences.en: Literally, by putting your kids into kind of something they might one day grow up and become.
sentences.zh: 字面意思，就是把你的孩子打扮成他们未来某天长大后可能会成为的样子。

sentences.en: It's rather perverse, but there we are.
sentences.zh: 这有点反常，但现实就是这样。

sentences.en: This is Professor Jonathan Fares.
sentences.zh: 这是 Jonathan Fares 教授。

sentences.en: And he says that in the United Kingdom, the equivalent of the sailor suit was a little plaid kilt with a suit jacket over it.
sentences.zh: 他说在英国，水手服的对应款式是一条小苏格兰格呢短裙，外面套一件西装夹克。

sentences.en: Because this was once the uniform of the Catholic soldiers in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 因为这曾是苏格兰天主教士兵的制服。

sentences.en: It was a very popular choice if you were a wealthy family to dress your kids in.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个富裕的家庭，把孩子打扮成这样是非常受欢迎的选择。

sentences.en: To be like little soldiers?
sentences.zh: 就像小士兵一样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, little soldiers, little tough boys and girls.
sentences.zh: 对，小士兵，坚强的小男孩和小女孩。

sentences.en: The little plaid kilt was common for upper-class boys.
sentences.zh: 小苏格兰格呢短裙在上流社会的小男孩中很常见。

sentences.en: And then, this uniform spread to girls when they were also able to attend school.
sentences.zh: 后来，当女孩们也能去上学时，这种制服也普及到了女孩身上。

sentences.en: Your next article of interest is plaid.
sentences.zh: 你的下一个关注焦点是格子呢。

sentences.en: Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: Radiotopia。
